metadata.task: Query Protocol Design for Token-Efficient Database I/O

baseline.top_pain_point: Reading 6000-token index.json to find 200 tokens of useful data

tiered_index.description: Progressive disclosure index system. Agents start at Level 0 and drill down only as needed. Each level costs more tokens but provides more detail. The system eliminates the current pattern of reading full 6000-token indexes for simple lookups.

levels.name: SUMMARY.json
levels.purpose: Instant orientation: what is in this directory?

properties.last_updated: string — ISO date of most recent entry

example.purpose: Shared knowledge entries documenting methods, tools, and lessons learned

levels.generation_method: Auto-generated by generate_index.py from source files. Regenerated on any entry change via pre-commit hook.

levels.name: INDEX_COMPACT.json
levels.purpose: Discovery: scan all entries by title/category/date to find relevant ones

items.description: Columnar format: [id, title, category, date] per entry, one line each

levels.generation_method: Auto-generated from source file frontmatter. Columnar array format (header + value arrays) saves ~44% tokens vs repeated JSON keys. One line per entry.
levels.token_cost_vs_baseline: ~500 tokens for 31 entries vs 6093 tokens (91.7% reduction)

levels.name: Full index.json (current format)
levels.purpose: Complete metadata including tags, builds_on, confidence, status — only when Level 0-1 are insufficient
levels.schema: Current index.json schema (unchanged for backward compatibility)
levels.generation_method: Existing files. Eventually auto-generated from source files + SQLite DB.
levels.token_cost_vs_baseline: Same as current (6093 tokens). Rarely needed under new protocol.
levels.deprecation_note: Agents should avoid reading Level 2 directly. Use query() or search() via MCP instead, which returns only matching entries with requested fields.

levels.name: Individual file reads
levels.purpose: Full content of a specific entry — only when deep analysis is required
levels.schema: Markdown with YAML frontmatter (current format, unchanged)
levels.generation_method: Source of truth. Human-authored. Never auto-generated.
levels.token_cost_vs_baseline: On-demand per entry. Average KB entry: 2224 tokens.

agent_workflow: 2. If needed, read INDEX_COMPACT.json (Level 1, ~500 tokens) to find specific entries
3. If filtering by tags/builds_on/confidence needed, use MCP search() which queries SQLite (avoids Level 2 entirely)
4. Read individual files (Level 3) only for entries identified in steps 2-3

root_summary.description: A single SUMMARY.json at repository root aggregates all directory summaries

query_interface.description: Six operations providing complete CRUD + search functionality with token-efficient defaults. All operations support field projection and token budgets. Operations map 1:1 to MCP tools.

operations.name: summary
operations.description: Returns Level 0 repository or directory summary. Cheapest possible orientation.

resource_type.description: Which resource type to summarize. 'all' returns the root summary.

response.purpose: Shared knowledge entries documenting methods, tools, and lessons learned

operations.name: list
operations.description: Returns Level 1 compact listing of all entries of a given type. For scanning/browsing.

fields.description: Fields to include in each entry. Fewer fields = fewer tokens.

limit.description: Max entries to return. null = all.

max_tokens.description: Token budget. Results truncated to fit.

operations.name: query
operations.description: Filtered retrieval with field projection. Returns entries matching criteria with only requested fields. Uses SQLite indexes for efficient filtering.

filters.description: Key-value filters. Supports: category, tags (any match), status, confidence, date_after, date_before, team, builds_on

operations.name: search
operations.description: Full-text search using SQLite FTS5. Supports BM25 ranking, phrase search, prefix search, boolean operators (AND/OR/NOT). Searches across titles, tags, categories, and optionally content summaries.

text.description: Search query. Supports FTS5 syntax: 'database AND coordination', '"exact phrase"', 'prefix*'

resource_types.description: Which resource types to search across

search_scope.description: 'metadata' searches titles/tags/categories. 'content' searches full text. 'all' searches everything.

results.title: SQLite WAL for Shared Agent State

operations.name: read
operations.description: Reads a specific entry by ID. Supports field projection to return only requested sections. This is the Level 3 access — full content retrieval.

fields.description: Fields/sections to return. For KB entries: 'metadata', 'summary', 'context', 'method', 'result', 'lessons', 'recommendations', 'content' (full). For SOPs: 'metadata', 'steps', 'checklist'.

brief.description: If true, returns metadata + summary only (no full content). Equivalent to fields=['metadata','summary'].

max_tokens.description: Token budget. Sections returned in priority order (summary > result > recommendations > lessons > method > context) until budget exhausted.

token_cost_estimate.vs_baseline: 80 (brief) vs 2224 avg full entry (96.4% reduction for brief reads)

response.recommendations: Use SQLite with WAL mode for embedded structured storage. Use JSON files for human-readable config. Consider LMDB for high-throughput key-value needs.

operations.name: write
operations.description: Creates a new entry with auto-assigned ID, auto-generated index entries, and validation. Replaces the manual template-copy-fill-index-update workflow.

content.description: Entry content. Required fields vary by resource_type. For KB: {title, category, tags, team, content_sections: {context, method, result, lessons, recommendations}}.

validate_only.description: If true, validates without writing. Returns validation result.

token_cost_estimate.vs_baseline: 200 vs 14561 (98.6% reduction — eliminates template read + full index read-modify-write cycle)

example.call: write(resource_type='kb', content={title:'Query Protocol Design', category:'architecture', tags:['database','token-efficiency','mcp'], team:'B2-Beta', content_sections:{context:'...', result:'...'}})

token_budget.description: Every query operation accepts a max_tokens parameter that bounds the response size. The query engine returns the highest-value results that fit within the budget, using relevance ranking to prioritize.

enforcement_rules.description: Estimate tokens using chars/4 approximation (validated in B2-Alpha baseline). Applied before serialization.

When results exceed budget, truncate in priority order: (1) reduce fields to minimum (id, title), (2) reduce result count, (3) truncate long text fields. Never return partial entries — either include all requested fields for an entry or omit the entry entirely.
Every response includes tokens_used and truncated fields so agents know if they received complete results.
Even with a tiny budget, always return at least one result with id and title. Minimum useful response: ~15 tokens.
When budget is exceeded, response includes: truncated=true, total_matches (so agent knows how many results exist), and a suggested higher budget.

standard_envelope.tokens_used: integer — estimated tokens consumed by this response
standard_envelope.total_matches: integer — total entries matching the query (may be > returned)
standard_envelope.returned_count: integer — number of entries in this response
standard_envelope.truncated: boolean — true if results were cut to fit budget

session_budget_tracking.description: Optional: track cumulative token usage across a session. Agents can query their running total and adjust query budgets accordingly.

fields.session_tokens_total: integer — cumulative tokens consumed across all queries this session
fields.session_queries_count: integer — number of queries issued this session

output_formats.name: json
output_formats.description: Standard structured JSON output. Default format. Best for programmatic consumption and complex nested data.
output_formats.use_case: Default for all operations. Use when agents need to process structured results.

output_formats.name: csv
output_formats.description: Columnar CSV format. Header row + value rows. Eliminates repeated key names. Ideal for bulk listings where all entries have the same fields.
output_formats.token_efficiency: 0.2x (80% fewer tokens than JSON for tabular data)
output_formats.use_case: list() operations, bulk scans, any query returning many entries with uniform fields. Preferred format for INDEX_COMPACT files.
output_formats.example:
id,title,category,date
KB-0008,Data Storage Methods,methodology,2026-03-10
KB-0031,Data Reform Analysis,methodology,2026-03-11
output_formats.token_savings_detail: 31 KB entries: JSON = ~1200 tokens, CSV = ~250 tokens. Savings come from eliminating 31 x 4 = 124 repeated key names.

output_formats.name: tsv
output_formats.description: Tab-separated values. Like CSV but tab-delimited. Grep-friendly, diff-friendly. Best for manifest-style output where values may contain commas.
output_formats.use_case: Manifest files, grep-based filtering, piping to command-line tools. Directory .manifest files use this format.
output_formats.example:
KB-0008	Data Storage Methods	methodology	2026-03-10
KB-0031	Data Reform Analysis	methodology	2026-03-11

output_formats.name: summary
output_formats.description: Natural language summary. Ultra-compact orientation format. Returns a human-readable paragraph instead of structured data.
output_formats.token_efficiency: 0.05x (95% fewer tokens than JSON for orientation)
output_formats.use_case: summary() operation. Agent orientation at session start. Quick status checks.
output_formats.example: Knowledge base: 31 entries across 5 categories (methodology, optimization, integration, tool-usage, architecture). Last updated 2026-03-11. Most active categories: methodology (12 entries), optimization (7 entries). Recent: KB-0031 Data Reform Analysis, KB-0030 Infrastructure Self-Reflection.

output_formats.name: ndjson
output_formats.description: Newline-delimited JSON. One complete JSON object per line. Stream-parseable, append-friendly, git-diff-friendly.
output_formats.token_efficiency: 0.85x (15% fewer tokens than formatted JSON — no indentation/nesting overhead)
output_formats.use_case: Streaming results, append-only logs, incremental index updates. Used for changelog feeds and real-time coordination data.

mcp_tools.description: Returns Level 0 repository or directory summary. Cheapest orientation tool (~50 tokens). Start every session with this.
Full-text search with FTS5 ranking, field projection, and token budgeting. Primary discovery tool. Replaces reading index.json files.

text.description: Search query (FTS5 syntax: AND/OR/NOT, phrases, prefixes)

filters.description: Structured filters: {category, tags, status, confidence, date_after, date_before, team}

data.title: SQLite WAL for Shared Agent State

mcp_tools.description: Reads a specific entry by ID with optional field/section projection. Supports brief mode for metadata-only reads.

fields.description: Sections to return. KB: metadata, summary, context, method, result, lessons, recommendations, content

response.summary: Evaluates SQLite, LMDB, JSON, MessagePack, and Redis for agent data storage. Recommends SQLite with WAL mode as primary.

mcp_tools.description: Creates a new entry with auto-assigned ID, validation, and automatic index updates. Eliminates the template-copy-fill-index-update workflow.
Structured metadata query with filters, projection, pagination, and token budgeting. For when you know what you are looking for (vs search for text matching).

common_workflows.description: The top 5 most common agent operations mapped to the new protocol, with token cost comparisons.

workflows.name: Session Orientation
workflows.current_pattern: Read CLAUDE.md + index.json + recent team logs = 3-5 file reads, ~12,000 tokens

workflows.name: Find Relevant KB Entries
workflows.current_pattern: Read knowledge-base/index.json (6093 tokens), scan entries array, then read matching files
workflows.new_pattern: repo_search(text='topic', resource_types=['kb'], fields=['id','title','summary']) = 1 MCP call, ~100 tokens

workflows.name: Read Specific Entry Recommendations
workflows.current_pattern: Read full KB entry file (avg 2224 tokens) even when only recommendations section needed

workflows.name: Create New KB Entry
workflows.current_pattern: Read template (146 tokens) + write content + read index (6093 tokens) + rewrite index (6093 tokens) = 14,561 tokens

workflows.name: List All SOPs
workflows.new_pattern: repo_query(resource_type='sops', fields=['id','title'], format='csv') = 1 MCP call, ~200 tokens

implementation_architecture.description: How the query protocol layers onto the existing repository infrastructure.

layers.contents: Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, JSON source/SOP files
layers.role: Canonical data. Human-readable, git-tracked. Never modified by query layer.
Generated artifact. Tables: entries (all resource types), entries_fts (FTS5 virtual table), tags (junction table), relationships (builds_on graph). Regenerated from source files by generate_index.py.
Pre-generated Level 0 and Level 1 files. Used when SQLite unavailable or for ultra-fast reads. Git-committed for instant access.
5 MCP tools (repo_summary, repo_search, repo_query, repo_read, repo_write) that query SQLite, fall back to static cache, and enforce token budgets.

implementation_architecture.data_flow: Source files --> generate_index.py --> [repo_index.db + SUMMARY.json + INDEX_COMPACT.json] --> MCP server --> Agent queries

tables: entries (id TEXT PK, resource_type TEXT, title TEXT, category TEXT, date TEXT, team TEXT, status TEXT, confidence TEXT, file_path TEXT, summary TEXT, content TEXT, meta_json TEXT)
entries_fts USING fts5(title, category, tags_text, summary, content=entries, content_rowid=rowid)
tags (entry_id TEXT, tag TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(entry_id, tag))
relationships (source_id TEXT, target_id TEXT, rel_type TEXT DEFAULT 'builds_on')

design_principles: Source files remain the single source of truth; all indexes are generated artifacts
Every operation has a token budget; no unbounded reads
Progressive disclosure: start cheap (Level 0), drill down only as needed
Backward compatible: existing file reads still work; new protocol is additive
Format-aware: CSV for bulk data, JSON for structured data, summary for orientation
Zero external dependencies: everything uses Python stdlib (sqlite3, json, csv)
summary.key_insight: The protocol achieves 93-99% token savings not through compression or encoding tricks, but by changing the access pattern: agents read summaries instead of full indexes, query for specific fields instead of reading entire files, and write through an atomic tool instead of a multi-step template-copy-index-update cycle. The tiered index system means most agent operations never touch more than 50-500 tokens of index data, down from 6000-28000 tokens today.
